text.p: MidAmerican Energy Holdings Co said Friday it settled its lawsuit against Nebraska Public Power District (NPPD) concerning the operation of Cooper Nuclear Station in Brownville, Neb., which is owned by NPPD.

Under the settlement, MidAmerican and NPPD will attempt to negotiate a new power sales contract. If a new agreement is not reached, NPPD will make a cash payment of an undisclosed amount to MidAmerican and amend the existing power sales contract, MidAmerican said.
MidAmerican pays one-half of Cooper Station's costs and receives one-half of the electrical output from the plant under a long-term power sales contract.

In May 1995, MidAmerican filed a complaint against NPPD in U.S. Federal Court in Des Moines, alleging that NPPD failed to operate Cooper in accordance with the power sales contract and other legal obligations. It also alleged that Cooper experienced unplanned and extended outages.
MidAmerican had sought in its suit to recover money damages from NPPD. A trial was to begin on June 16.
